- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model tends to overshoot; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at 80–82 to prevent overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.2) and forecast is low, consider a 1–3% upward bias to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves after 10–15 days of high prices; apply a 1–3% downward bias for 3–5 day horizon.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is > 82 and true outcome drops below 75, adjust next 5 days downward by 1–2% per day.  
- Sentiment + price history: if sentiment is negative and price is trending up, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid sentiment-driven overcorrection.
